title: POC weekly throughput/latency scrub + playbook - NovaHelix
summary: Week 3 POC review vs incumbent baseline. Redwood shows lower p95 latency on short prompts but higher variance on long sequences; throughput improvements after batching tweaks. Agreed next steps: run dedicated slot test, share exact load script and perf config, security doc handoff, and schedule canary with production-like traffic patterns.
action_items: Maya Chen | Share perf-config.json and the load script link | 2027-06-04
Ethan Park | Spin up dedicated slot for 3-hour run and capture perf counters | 2027-06-07
Ravi Patel | Provide sample production request distribution and top 10 prompt prefixes | 2027-06-05
Priya Rao | Add KV-cache warmup step to benchmark and re-run | 2027-06-06
next_steps: Redwood to provision a dedicated slot and run 3-hour throughput test against NovaHelix traffic mix
Customer to validate output quality for quantized 4-bit run on 500 random prompts
Exchange security checklist and SOC2 snapshot via secure link
Schedule canary run with 10% production traffic in two weeks
meeting_header: Date: 2027-06-02 | Time: 08:00 PT | Duration: 52 minutes | Recording: Yes | Platform: Zoom | Summary: POC weekly sync (throughput/latency) vs baseline provider
transcript:
[00:00] Maya Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. We're on for the weekly POC scrub, gonna run through the latest runs and then a routing/playbook proposal.
[00:12] Liam Torres: Yeah thanks, Maya. We had a few stakeholders on standby, Amira and Ravi are here to talk infra.
[00:20] Amira Haddad: morning, quick heads up we observed some spikes yesterday around 3pm — tail latency p99-ish.
[00:28] Ethan Park: okay noted. We'll pull the logs. So quick agenda — run summary, delta vs your incumbent (CloudServe), then tuning notes and playbook.
[00:41] Ravi Patel: before that, we got the baseline traces — just to confirm the comparisons are apples-to-apples? Our baseline uses 8k token truncation and a custom KV cache layer.
[00:53] Priya Rao: (overlap) yep, we tried to mirror truncation and warmup, there might be small diffs in batcher behaviour though.
[01:00] Maya Chen: Right — our bench used the same 8k config but default continuous-batching; we changed batch size from 32 to 16 yesterday which reduced tail.
[01:15] Sofia Marin: quick Q: what do you mean by "tail" — p95 vs p99? Which metric should we focus on for user experience?
[01:23] Ethan Park: good call — we typically monitor p50, p95, p99 and token-per-second. For chat-like UX p95 is most representative, p99 matters for SLA.
[01:34] Liam Torres: okay show us the numbers then.
[01:36] Ethan Park: slide 1 — week-over-week. For short prompts (<256 tokens) Redwood p95 is 28ms vs CloudServe 45ms, p99 90ms vs 130ms. For long sequences (~3k tokens) p95 420ms vs 380ms (so we regressed slightly).
[01:56] Amira Haddad: hmm that long-seq regression is concerning, we have workflows that hit 3k regularly.
[02:02] Priya Rao: that was with default kv warmup disabled; when we enabled prefix KV warmup the long-seq p95 dropped to 360ms, closer to incumbent.
[02:12] Ravi Patel: can you explain what "kv warmup" is? the transcription sometimes says...
[02:16] Ethan Park: sure — it's the process of warming the key-value cache so the initial tokens are in GPU memory; without it the first few steps read from slower path.
[02:26] Maya Chen: also, quantization had an effect — 4-bit quant reduced throughput variance but we saw a 0.8% delta in BLEU-style similarity over the eval set. Not huge but worth QA.
[02:39] Sofia Marin: we can't accept accuracy regressions >1% so that's borderline.
[02:42] Ethan Park: understood — we can run a mixed-precision run to validate.
[02:47] [03:00] Ethan Park: moving on to throughput — with batching tuned to 24 we achieved 1,200 rps sustained on the dedicated test harness vs baseline 900 rps. But the CPU preshow on our side caused jitter.
[03:18] Amira Haddad: CPU preshow?
[03:20] Priya Rao: yeah that's the process that prepares tokenization and small precompute on CPU; we've seen some multi-thread contention in our lab VMs.
[03:30] Ravi Patel: can you dump the exact run command? we want to replicate locally.
[03:33] Maya Chen: yes — action item, we'll share the perf-config.json and the load script link.
[03:39] [03:50] Liam Torres: Also curious about cost — you mentioned dedicated slot cost vs hosted. If we need dedicated for predictable latency how big is the delta on monthly run?
[03:58] Maya Chen: rough ballpark — dedicated reserved slot is ~1.8x per-hour of on-demand hosted for comparable perf; but unit cost per token was lower due to batching and KV cache. We'll send estimated TCO after we know their traffic profile.
[04:12] Sofia Marin: please include memory/PCI-e stats — our infra team cares about GPU memory cliffs.
[04:18] Ethan Park: will include NVLink and memory footprint graphs.
[04:23] [04:30] Priya Rao: quick interjection — routing and fallback: we propose primary on the low-latency variant and fallback to a cheaper quantized model if queue depth exceeds threshold. This reduces cost while preserving SLOs.
[04:43] Ravi Patel: fallback is fine but need strong quality checks. Can we A/B for 5%?
[04:47] Maya Chen: yes — canary at 5-10% is our recommendation. Also we'll configure automatic rollback on quality drift.
[04:56] [05:10] Ethan Park: I want to call out an anomaly from the last run — a steady increase in token latency correlating with KV eviction at ~2h mark. We need to test a larger cache and also a periodic warmup.
[05:24] Amira Haddad: eviction? do you mean memory eviction?
[05:27] Ethan Park: yes, when GPU memory pressure hits a threshold, the runtime swaps out parts of the KV cache, causing slow-path reads and latency spikes.
[05:36] Liam Torres: so solution is bigger cache or different eviction policy? cost tradeoff?
[05:41] Priya Rao: both: increasing cache size reduces evictions but uses more memory; we can also tune eviction to LRU with a heavier prefetch. We'll propose numbers.
[05:51] [06:05] Sofia Marin: about the dedicated slot request — what's the minimum time for you to stand it up and run a 3-hour test?
[06:11] Maya Chen: we can provision within 48 hours; best-effort to run the long test within a week. Ethan will kick it off.
[06:18] Ethan Park: noted. We'll run a 3-hour run with your production mix and capture p50/p95/p99, token-per-second, and memory counters every 5 minutes.
[06:29] Ravi Patel: please include a step that replays our top 10 prompt prefixes, those are heavy hitters.
[06:34] Maya Chen: noted — action item for Ravi to provide prefixes.
[06:37] [06:45] Amira Haddad: security question — do you have a SOC2 snapshot and encryption-at-rest details? We need to pass this to procurement.
[06:52] Maya Chen: yes, we have SOC2 Type II and can share a redacted snapshot; we also support customer-managed keys and HSM integrations. We'll send the security packet.
[07:03] Sofia Marin: perfect. Also, for legal, we need retention and deletion timelines.
[07:07] Maya Chen: standard retention is configurable, we'll align with your compliance team.
[07:12] [07:20] Ethan Park: back to perf — there's one more variable: request routing. If we route by latency vs cost we can bias towards low-latency regional variants. That improved p95 8% in our testing.
[07:33] Liam Torres: do you support region pinning for privacy reasons?
[07:36] Priya Rao: yes, private deployments support region pinning and VPC peering for on-prem. For hosted we have regional endpoints.
[07:45] [07:55] Maya Chen: ok wrapping up — recap: Redwood shows clear wins on short prompts, marginal regressions on long sequences that we can mitigate with KV warmup and larger cache; throughput looks good after batching tune. Next: dedicated slot run, share perf configs, QA on quantized outputs, security doc handoff, schedule canary.
[08:18] Ravi Patel: sounds good. Can you also include the exact inc- baseline elastic scaling config used for comparison?
[08:24] Ethan Park: yes we'll attach baseline config in the perf artifact.
[08:28] Sofia Marin: thanks team, let's aim for the dedicated run early next week.
[08:31] Maya Chen: thanks all. I'll follow up with the links and invite for the canary planning.
[08:36] [08:40] Meeting ended.
